newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina told a civic reception in New York on Tuesday that issues relating to Ganges water sharing with India, refugee problem with Myanmar and asset sharing with Pakistan could be resolved through bilateral discussion.

Police on Tuesday confiscated the house of retired army major Shariful Haq Dalim, one of the main accused of the killing of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. Dalim is absconding and the government is trying to trace him.
Vice-President of Asian Development Bank (ADB) Bong-Suh Lee arrives in Dhaka on Thursday for a four-day trip to discuss the bank's lending programmes with Bangladesh leaders.
The Dhaka University authorities and the Dhaka Metropolitan Police have jointly chalked out a "crash programme" to wipe out terrorism from the campus.
Bangladesh has decided to be a candidate for a non-permanent seat of the Unitd Nations Security Council for the term 2000-2001.

Finance Minister S A M S Kibria on Tuesday charged the previous BNP government with "criminal neglect" of the power sector that, he said, was severely reducing the economic prospects. "The gretest harm they had done was not taking any step for the power sector," he told a meeting of the foreign investors'chamber.
Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd on Tuesday launched a Mudaraba Savings Bond Scheme to encourage savings.
